skill.name: architecture-navigator
skill.description: Understand and navigate the DevPrep AI 7-folder architecture. Use this skill when asked about code organization, where to place new features, what modules exist, or when starting development tasks that need architecture context. Auto-triggers on keywords like "where should", "add module", "architecture", "structure", "organize", "place code", "what modules".
skill.summary: Navigate DevPrep AI code organization and place work in the correct architecture layer.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: Static findings were reviewed in context and were false positives from Markdown formatting or a read-only architecture scanner. No prompt injection, network access, destructive behavior, credential access, or exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: 6. **Types Are Global**: Put shared types in types/ to avoid circular dependencies
1. **Is it a route/page?** → `app/` (but keep minimal, import from modules/)
| "Where should social login go?" | `modules/auth/` - Feature-specific authentication logic |
| "Where should I add payment processing?" | `modules/payments/` - New feature module for payment do
| "Where do reusable buttons go?" | `shared/components/ui/Button.tsx` - Reusable UI component |
| "Where's the Claude AI integration?" | `lib/claude/` - External service integration |
| "Where should shopping cart state go?" | `store/cartStore.ts` - Global state management |
| "Where do API types go?" | `types/ai/api.ts` - Shared TypeScript definitions |
- ✅ Shared components are in `shared/`, not duplicated
1. Run `scripts/scan_architecture.sh` to generate current architecture map
The OAuth client setup (SDK wrapper) should go in `lib/oauth/client.ts` (external integration).
**Manual invocation:** Use `/architecture` or explicitly request "scan the architecture".
4. **Reference rules**: Point to `architecture-rules.md` for detailed justification
2. **Notification State** → `store/uiStore.ts` (global state for managing active toasts)

content.value_statement: Large codebases make placement decisions slow and inconsistent. This skill maps DevPrep AI architecture and guides code placement with clear folder rules.
actual_capabilities: Scans the DevPrep AI frontend source tree with a bundled Bash script.
Summarizes modules, shared code, integrations, stores, types, styles, and routes.
Answers where new code should live using seven-folder placement rules.
Explains import direction rules and forbidden dependency patterns.
Helps validate whether routes, modules, shared code, and state follow documented boundaries.
limitations: Designed for DevPrep AI architecture conventions, not every project structure.
Requires local repository access for real-time scanning.
The scanner reports file counts and folders, not full dependency graphs.
Placement advice still needs developer judgment for ambiguous cross-cutting features.

use_cases.title: Place New Features
use_cases.description: Decide whether new work belongs in modules, shared, lib, store, types, styles, or app.

use_cases.title: Understand Existing Structure
use_cases.description: Generate a concise map of the current DevPrep AI frontend folders before starting work.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Drift
use_cases.description: Check whether routes stay thin, shared code stays reusable, and imports follow documented boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Scan the Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan the DevPrep AI architecture and summarize the seven main folders with current module counts.

prompt_templates.title: Place a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Where should I add a new payment history feature in DevPrep AI? Explain the folder choice and related files.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Change Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned file layout against the DevPrep AI architecture rules and flag any misplaced logic.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Boundary Questions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare module, shared, lib, and store placement for a global notification system. Recommend final paths and import flow.

output_examples.output: Social login belongs in the authentication module because it is feature-specific. Provider SDK setup belongs in lib because it wraps an external integration.
The skill can run the architecture scanner, list current feature modules, show file counts, and identify key shared locations.

output_examples.input: Does this page contain too much logic?
output_examples.output: The skill checks whether the route stays minimal and recommends moving business logic into the matching feature module when needed.

best_practices: Run the scan before making placement decisions in an unfamiliar checkout.
Ask for exact paths and the rule that supports each recommendation.
Use the reference rules when reviewing imports across architecture layers.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill as a general architecture standard for unrelated repositories.
Do not place business logic in app routes when a feature module should own it.
Do not treat generated folder counts as proof that dependencies are correct.

faq.question: What project is this skill designed for?
faq.answer: It is designed for the DevPrep AI frontend and its seven-folder architecture.

faq.question: Does it modify source files?
faq.answer: No. The scanner reads local folders and prints an architecture summary.

faq.question: Can it answer where new files should go?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses documented folder rules to recommend specific placement paths.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Can it detect every architecture violation?
faq.answer: No. It gives folder and rule guidance, but it does not build a full dependency graph.

faq.question: When should I run the scanner?
faq.answer: Run it before placement decisions, architecture reviews, or questions about existing modules.
